claim: On the current local Linux JDK 27 provider, an open process-directory SecureDirectoryStream reads live status and reports an IOException after that actual process exits, retaining failure rather than substituting a memory value.
required_behavior: Sample the owned process tree without reading a replacement process after PID reuse. Preserve inaccessible, missing and exited-process observations separately from a valid zero memory observation.

local_project_observation.LinuxMemory: Existing host sampler reads named counters with JDK Properties and checked byte conversion; it does not sample owned process RSS.
local_project_observation.LinuxProcessTree: Existing members() reads the owned inner cgroup.procs list; it does not bind later proc reads to process identity.
local_project_observation.LinuxSupervisor: Existing directory() supplies the owned outer cgroup observation boundary.

decision_members: Properties.getProperty("VmRSS") from the descriptor-relative status reader
IOException type and message for failed descriptor-relative access
candidate.selection: Not yet selected as a production sampler. This evaluates the platform candidate only.

authoritative_contracts.supports: Relative operations use the already-open directory, including when that directory is moved or replaced; support depends on the provider.
Operations through an open proc process-directory descriptor do not act on a replacement process after PID reuse; dead-process access normally fails with ESRCH.

probe.process_cleanup: The real child JVM receives input EOF, exits zero and is reaped; finally also forcibly destroys/reaps it if an earlier operation fails. Readers, channels and directory stream use try-with-resources.

limitations: This is a direct platform-candidate evaluation, not a final caller-facing sampler recreation or a production behavior gate.
It does not force PID reuse. The non-retargeting guarantee comes from the documented kernel contract; the probe exercises the JDK provider and actual process-exit behavior.

Opening a process directory after enumerating a PID can already encounter a replacement. A final sampler must verify ownership using a descriptor-relative cgroup observation and reconcile changing membership before accepting the sample.
Summed RSS is approximate sampled residency: shared pages can be counted per process and short-lived peaks can be missed. It is not cgroup memory consumption or an exact lifetime peak.
Missing VmRSS, malformed or overflowing counters, inaccessible processes, unsupported providers and membership churn still need exact public-operation acceptance cases.
Native release-runner x86-64/ARM64 composition, memory admission/control and Cargo/Bazel integration remain unaccepted by this probe.
next_gate: Finish candidate comparison and a bounded ownership/membership contract; exercise the exact caller-facing Java sampler and declared dependencies in a fresh empty folder before production edits.
